title: A wet chemical extraction protocol for measuring biogenic silica in sediments of marginal seas and open ocean
author: Zhu, Liu, et al.

steps.title: Freeze‑dry sediment samples
steps.instruction: Store approximately 200 g of wet sediment at –20 °C for 12 h, then place in a freeze‑dryer for 48–72 h until completely dry.

steps.title: Prepare slides for micrography
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 mg of dried sediment into a 15 mL centrifuge tube, add 1 mL of 1.0 M HCl and 1 mL of 30 % H₂O₂, and incubate for 2 h to remove organic matter and carbonates. Wash the residue three times with 5 mL Milli‑Q water, then add 1 mL Milli‑Q water and mix with an electric mixer at 1000 rpm for 10 s. Transfer the well‑mixed suspension onto a glass microscope slide with a pipette and examine under an optical microscope to identify biogenic silica types (phytoliths, diatoms, sponge spicules, radiolarians, silicoflagellates).

steps.title: Select appropriate alkaline extraction solution
steps.instruction: Based on microscopy, choose 0.1 M Na₂CO₃ for samples dominated by diatoms, phytoliths and silicoflagellates (≈90 % of bSi) or 0.5 M NaOH for samples containing >10 % sponge spicules or radiolarians, or when total bSi content exceeds 10 %. Approximate bSi content using Fig. 1 if needed.

steps.title: Gently homogenize freeze‑dried sediment
steps.instruction: Using an agate mortar and a lab spatula, gently grind the freeze‑dried sediment to achieve a uniform fine powder without pulverizing the biosiliceous structures. Store the homogenized material in a desiccator at room temperature.

steps.title: Weigh sediment into extraction tube
steps.instruction: Place a 50 mL fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) or polypropylene centrifuge tube on an analytical balance, add 30–150 mg of the homogenized sediment, and record the exact mass.

steps.title: Add alkaline solution
steps.instruction: Add 40 mL of the selected alkaline solution (0.1 M Na₂CO₃ or 0.5 M NaOH) to the tube containing the weighed sediment.

steps.title: Initial mixing of sediment and solution
steps.instruction: Mix the tube with an electric mixer at 1000 rpm for 30 s to ensure thorough suspension of the sediment.

steps.title: Perform alkaline extraction
steps.instruction: Seal the tube tightly, place it in a water bath pre‑heated to 85 °C, and shake at 100 rpm. Extract for 8 h for diatom‑rich samples or 10–12 h for sponge/radiolarian‑rich samples.

substeps.instruction: At each 1‑hour interval, remove the tube, centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 5 min.
Using a pipette, withdraw 200 µL of the supernatant (adjust to 100–500 µL if Si concentration is high) for dissolved Si analysis.
Store the withdrawn leachate in a 15 mL polypropylene tube at 4 °C until measurement.
After sampling, remix the remaining sediment‑solution mixture with the electric mixer at 1000 rpm for 30 s, then return the tube to the 85 °C water bath to continue extraction.

steps.title: Measure dissolved silica concentration
steps.instruction: Determine Si in each leachate aliquot using the molybdenum‑blue photometric method on a UV‑spectrophotometer (alternatively ICP‑OES or a nutrient auto‑analyser). Prepare a working standard curve ranging from 0 to 20 µM (dilute the alkaline extract by a factor of 75 so that the final Si concentration is ≤15 µM). Calculate biogenic silica content from the measured Si concentrations.
